page: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance provisions two virtual CPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading enabled across an x86_64 architecture. Hardware cache allocations include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage, requiring remote EBS volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with no bundled GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance alongside predictable constraints in multi-threaded execution due to its two-thread limit. In stress-ng testing, single-core processing rated in the top 25 percent, while multi-core throughput dropped to the bottom 25 percent. Geekbench evaluation reflected an average single-core score of 1643.0 and a multi-core score of 2024.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 31.33 GB/sec, while write operations measured 21.46 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 2.28 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 2.87 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r6a.large offers an accessible entry point to AMD-based memory-dense infrastructure without the commitment of higher core counts. Because the allocation relies on a single dual-threaded physical core, high-concurrency tasks experience clear throughput boundaries. The instance is suitable for intermediate in-memory caching tiers, small relational databases, staging environments, and memory-intensive microservices requiring modest compute power.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is a memory-optimized virtual instance built on the Nitro platform and powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor. Operating on an x86_64 architecture, it delivers two dedicated vCPUs from a single physical execution core paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The configuration lacks integrated local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network capacity without GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-threaded CPU metrics, while overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth reflect the limitations of its two-thread footprint, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 2024.0 and 2.28 million Redis SET operations per second. The r6a.large provides economical access to a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it an appropriate choice for small in-memory datastores, lightweight relational database workloads, and memory-dependent background workers.
